question: Should `sessions.list` intentionally change already-valid requests above 1000 into paginated 1000-row responses, or must existing one-call callers retain their requested result size?
rationale: The cap is a reasonable resource-control mechanism, but it changes the observable result of an existing schema-valid gateway request; analogous caps on other RPCs do not settle this RPC’s compatibility contract.

options.title: Approve the paginated 1000-row contract
options.body: Accept the compatibility change, document the upper bound and continuation requirement at the gateway API boundary, and merge with the regression coverage.

options.title: Preserve legacy result sizing
options.body: Keep requests above 1000 capable of returning their requested window and pursue resource protection at a boundary that does not silently truncate existing clients.

options.title: Pause for gateway-owner design
options.body: Defer the PR until an owner defines an explicit bounded-list API or migration path for callers that need more than 1000 entries.

recommendation.title: Approve the paginated 1000-row contract
recommendation.body: Accept the compatibility change, document the upper bound and continuation requirement at the gateway API boundary, and merge with the regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent gateway-bound work is the strongest available evidence for the list-cap design pattern, though ownership of this exact RPC remains low-confidence.
